FN-N3LNTJ-1
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 166
Committee: Fiscal Responsibility and Economic Development Sponsor: Senator Sam Givhan
Analyst: Jennifer Farish Date: 04/19/2023
Senate Bill 166 as introduced allows the Cities of Huntsville and Montgomery to establish one
or more self-help business improvement districts managed by a district management corporation
comprised of a board of directors of at least 3 members (, but not more than 13) to provide
supplemental services to promote the economic growth of the district or to increase tourism in
the municipality. The members of the board shall not be compensated but may receive
reimbursement for actual expenses relating to board activity paid from the special assessment
collected. A district management corporation under the provisions of this bill would be exempt
from corporate income and franchise taxes as well as state and local sales, use, license, gross
receipts, and ad valorem taxes. The impact of these exemptions on state and local tax receipts
would depend on such things as the value of the property involved and the cost of any
improvements. Supplemental services and improvements within the district would be funded by
special assessments authorized pursuant to the provisions of this bill, against the owners of real
property in the district excluding single-family, owner-occupied residential property and all
property of utilities other than land and retail storage and office facilities within the district. The
cities would not be prohibited from including a self-help business improvement district within
the bounds of any area or zone which has as one of its purposes the construction of
improvements or rehabilitation of properties. The provisions of this bill would increase the
administrative obligations of the cities to hold public hearings as required prior to the creation,
modification, or dissolution of a self-help business improvement district.

FN-N3LNTJ-2
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 166
Committee: Economic Development and Sponsor: Senator Sam Givhan
Tourism
Analyst: Jennifer Farish Date: 05/01/2023
Senate Bill 166 as passed the Senate would allow Class 3 Municipalities, by ordinance, to
establish one or more "self-help business improvement districts" and levy a special assessment
against the owners of real property or certain businesses within the district, for up to five years.
This bill provides that the revenues from this assessment would be used to provide supplemental
services including security, sanitation and parking in the district through the operation of a
district management corporation, provided for by this bill.
This bill provides that the members of the board of such corporation shall not be compensated
but may be reimbursed for actual expenses relating to board activity, paid from the special
assessment. This bill would exempt such corporation from state income and franchise taxes,
permit fees, and state and local sales, use, license, gross receipts, and ad valorem taxes, which
could decrease state and local receipts otherwise received by an undetermined amount
dependent the taxes that would have been collected absent this bill. This bill could increase the
administrative obligations of a municipality for holding public hearings, as required prior to the
creation or dissolution of such district.
